cues.en: Philosophers, dramatists, theologians

cues.en: have grappled with this question for centuries:

cues.zh: 人为什么会误入歧途？
cues.en: what makes people go wrong?

cues.zh: 有意思的是，我小时候就问过这个问题。
cues.en: Interestingly, I asked this question when I was a little kid.

cues.en: I grew up in the South Bronx, inner-city ghetto in New York,

cues.zh: 我周围满是邪恶，
cues.en: and I was surrounded by evil,

cues.en: as all kids are who grew up in an inner city.

cues.en: And I had friends who were really good kids,

cues.en: So when I read Robert Louis Stevenson, that wasn't fiction.

cues.en: The only question is, what was in the juice?

cues.zh: 更重要的是，善与恶之间那条界线——
cues.en: And more importantly, that line between good and evil --

cues.en: which privileged people like to think is fixed and impermeable,

cues.zh: 把他们自己划在善的一边，别人划在恶的一边——
cues.en: with them on the good side, the others on the bad side --

cues.zh: 我知道那条线是可以移动的，也是可以逾越的。
cues.en: I knew that line was movable, and it was permeable.

cues.zh: 好人也会被诱惑越过那条线，
cues.en: Good people could be seduced across that line,

cues.zh: 而在良好且某些罕见的情况下，坏孩子也能改过自新，
cues.en: and under good and some rare circumstances, bad kids could recover

cues.en: with help, with reform, with rehabilitation.

cues.en: So I want to begin with this wonderful illusion

cues.en: But let's look more deeply, and as we do,

cues.en: It also means "the morning star," in some scripture.

cues.zh: 显然，他违背了上帝，
cues.en: And apparently, he disobeyed God,

cues.en: and that's the ultimate disobedience to authority.

cues.en: He didn't do a good job of keeping it there though.

cues.zh: 对我来说，为理解人类设定了背景——

cues.en: who are transformed from good, ordinary people into perpetrators of evil.

cues.zh: 所以，路西法效应，尽管它聚焦于负面——
cues.en: So the Lucifer effect, although it focuses on the negatives --

cues.zh: 人们可能变成的负面，
cues.en: the negatives that people can become,

cues.en: not the negatives that people are --

cues.en: leads me to a psychological definition.

cues.zh: 关键在于：它关乎权力。
cues.en: And that's the key: it's about power.

cues.zh: 故意在心理上伤害他人，
cues.en: To intentionally harm people psychologically,

cues.en: to hurt people physically, to destroy people mortally, or ideas,

cues.en: "Don't blame us. It's not the system.

cues.en: they took pictures of everything, more than 1,000.

cues.en: The CIA was there.

cues.en: Interrogators from Titan Corporation, all there,

cues.en: and they're getting no information about the insurgency.

cues.en: to take the gloves off.

cues.en: How do psychologists try to understand such transformations of human character,

cues.en: if you believe that they were good soldiers

cues.zh: 有三种方式。主要的方式叫做倾向性归因。
cues.en: There are three ways. The main way is called dispositional.

cues.zh: 我们看人内在的东西，那些害群之马。
cues.en: We look at what's inside of the person, the bad apples.

cues.zh: 这是所有社会科学的基础，
cues.en: This is the foundation of all of social science,

cues.zh: 宗教的基础，战争的基础。
cues.en: the foundation of religion, the foundation of war.

cues.zh: 像我这样的社会心理学家走过来说，
cues.en: Social psychologists like me come along and say,

cues.zh: “没错，人是舞台上的演员，
cues.en: "Yeah, people are the actors on the stage,

cues.zh: 但你必须意识到情境的作用。
cues.en: but you'll have to be aware of the situation.

cues.zh: 角色阵容有哪些？戏服是什么？
cues.en: Who are the cast of characters? What's the costume?

cues.zh: 有没有舞台导演？
cues.en: Is there a stage director?"

cues.zh: 所以我们关注的是外部因素
cues.en: And so we're interested in what are the external factors

cues.en: around the individual -- the bad barrel?

cues.zh: 社会科学家止步于此，错过了关键点
cues.en: Social scientists stop there and they miss the big point

cues.zh: 这是我为阿布格莱布监狱做专家证人时发现的。
cues.en: that I discovered when I became an expert witness for Abu Ghraib.

cues.zh: 力量在于系统。
cues.en: The power is in the system.

cues.zh: 系统制造了腐蚀个体的情境，
cues.en: The system creates the situation that corrupts the individuals,

cues.zh: 而系统就是法律、政治、经济、文化背景。
cues.en: and the system is the legal, political, economic, cultural background.

cues.zh: 这正是坏桶制造者的力量所在。
cues.en: And this is where the power is of the bad-barrel makers.

cues.zh: 想改变一个人，就改变情境。
cues.en: If you want to change a person, change the situation.

cues.zh: 要改变它，你必须知道力量在哪里，在系统里。
cues.en: And to change it, you've got to know where the power is, in the system.

cues.zh: 所以路西法效应涉及理解
cues.en: So the Lucifer effect involves understanding

cues.en: human character transformations with these three factors.

cues.zh: 这是一种动态的相互作用。
cues.en: And it's a dynamic interplay.

cues.en: And what is the system that creates and maintains that situation?

cues.zh: 那是你必须做的决定，是个人的选择。
cues.en: That's a decision that you have to make, a personal thing.

cues.zh: 所以我想以积极的基调快速收尾。
cues.en: So I want to end very quickly on a positive note.

cues.zh: 英雄主义是邪恶的解药，
cues.en: Heroism as the antidote to evil,

cues.zh: 通过培养英雄式想象力，
cues.en: by promoting the heroic imagination,

cues.zh: 尤其是在我们的孩子身上，在我们的教育体系中。
cues.en: especially in our kids, in our educational system.

cues.zh: 我们希望孩子们想：“我是一个待命的英雄，
cues.en: We want kids to think, "I'm a hero in waiting,

cues.zh: 等待合适的时机出现，
cues.en: waiting for the right situation to come along,

cues.zh: 然后我会英勇行动。
cues.en: and I will act heroically.

cues.zh: 我这一生，现在要把焦点从邪恶上移开——
cues.en: My whole life, I'm now going to focus away from evil --

cues.zh: 那是我从小就一直在关注的——转向理解英雄。
cues.en: that I've been in since I was a kid -- to understanding heroes.

cues.zh: 英雄主义的平庸性。
cues.en: Banality of heroism.

cues.zh: 是普通人做出了英雄事迹。
cues.en: It's ordinary people who do heroic deeds.

cues.zh: 这是对汉娜·阿伦特“平庸之恶”的对应。
cues.en: It's the counterpoint to Hannah Arendt's "Banality of Evil."

cues.zh: 我们传统的社会英雄是错的，因为他们是例外。
cues.en: Our traditional societal heroes are wrong, because they are the exceptions.

cues.zh: 他们围绕这个来组织自己的生活。这就是为什么我们知道他们的名字。
cues.en: They organize their life around this. That's why we know their names.

cues.zh: 我们给孩子们树立的英雄榜样也选错了，
cues.en: Our kids' heroes are also wrong models for them,

cues.zh: 因为他们都有超自然的天赋。
cues.en: because they have supernatural talents.

cues.zh: 我们希望孩子明白，大多数英雄都是普通人，
cues.en: We want our kids to realize most heroes are everyday people,

cues.zh: 而英雄行为本身并不寻常。
cues.en: and the heroic act is unusual.

cues.zh: 这是 Joe Darby。
cues.en: This is Joe Darby.

cues.zh: 正是他阻止了你看到的那起虐囚事件，
cues.en: He was the one that stopped those abuses you saw,

cues.zh: 因为当他看到那些照片时，
cues.en: because when he saw those images,

cues.zh: 他把照片交给了高级调查官。
cues.en: he turned them over to a senior investigating officer.

cues.zh: 他只是个低级列兵，却阻止了这一切。
cues.en: He was a low-level private, and that stopped it.

cues.zh: 他是英雄吗？不是。
cues.en: Was he a hero? No.

cues.zh: 他们不得不把他藏起来，因为有人想杀他，
cues.en: They had to put him in hiding, because people wanted to kill him,

cues.zh: 还想杀他的母亲和妻子。
cues.en: and then his mother and his wife.

cues.zh: 整整三年，他们都在躲藏。
cues.en: For three years, they were in hiding.

cues.zh: 这位女士阻止了斯坦福监狱实验。
cues.en: This is the woman who stopped the Stanford Prison Study.

cues.zh: 当我说实验失控时，我就是那个监狱长。
cues.en: When I said it got out of control, I was the prison superintendent.

cues.zh: 我当时并不知道已经失控，我完全无动于衷。
cues.en: I didn't know it was out of control. I was totally indifferent.

cues.zh: 她看到那个疯人院，就说，
cues.en: She saw that madhouse and said,

cues.zh: “你知道吗，你们这样对待那些男孩太糟糕了。
cues.en: "You know what, it's terrible what you're doing to those boys.

cues.zh: 他们不是囚犯也不是狱警，他们是孩子，而你们要负责。”
cues.en: They're not prisoners nor guards, they're boys, and you are responsible."

cues.zh: 第二天我就终止了这项研究。
cues.en: And I ended the study the next day.

cues.zh: 好消息是，第二年我就娶了她。
cues.en: The good news is I married her the next year.

cues.zh: （笑声）
cues.en: (Laughter)

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)

cues.zh: 显然，我醒悟过来了。
cues.en: I just came to my senses, obviously.

cues.zh: 所以情境有能力做到[三件事]。
cues.en: So situations have the power to do [three things].

cues.zh: 但关键是，同样的情境
cues.en: But the point is, this is the same situation

cues.zh: 既能激发我们中一些人的敌意想象，
cues.en: that can inflame the hostile imagination in some of us,

cues.zh: 让我们成为邪恶的施害者，
cues.en: that makes us perpetrators of evil,

cues.zh: 也能激发另一些人的英雄想象。
cues.en: can inspire the heroic imagination in others.

cues.zh: 这是同一个情境，你要么站在这一边，要么站在那一边。
cues.en: It's the same situation and you're on one side or the other.

cues.zh: 大多数人都犯有袖手旁观的恶，
cues.en: Most people are guilty of the evil of inaction,

cues.zh: 因为你母亲说过，“别掺和。管好你自己的事。”
cues.en: because your mother said, "Don't get involved. Mind your own business."

cues.zh: 你得说：“妈妈，人类是我的事业。”
cues.en: And you have to say, "Mama, humanity is my business."

cues.zh: 那么英雄主义的心理学是——我们马上就要结束了——
cues.en: So the psychology of heroism is -- we're going to end in a moment --

cues.zh: 我们如何在新英雄课程中鼓励孩子们，
cues.en: how do we encourage children in new hero courses,

cues.zh: 这是我正与Matt Langdon合作的——他有一个英雄工作坊——
cues.en: that I'm working on with Matt Langdon -- he has a hero workshop --

cues.zh: 去培养这种英雄想象力，这种自我标签，
cues.en: to develop this heroic imagination, this self-labeling,

cues.zh: “我是一个待命的英雄”，并教他们技能。
cues.en: "I am a hero in waiting," and teach them skills.

cues.zh: 要成为英雄，你必须学会做一个离经叛道者，
cues.en: To be a hero, you have to learn to be a deviant,

cues.zh: 因为你总是在对抗群体的从众性。
cues.en: because you're always going against the conformity of the group.

cues.zh: 英雄是普通人，他们的社会行为却非凡。他们会行动。
cues.en: Heroes are ordinary people whose social actions are extraordinary. Who act.

cues.zh: 英雄主义的关键有两点。
cues.en: The key to heroism is two things.

cues.zh: 当其他人被动时，你必须行动。
cues.en: You have to act when other people are passive.

cues.zh: B：你必须以社会为中心行动，而不是以自我为中心。
cues.en: B: You have to act socio-centrically, not egocentrically.

cues.zh: 我想以一个众所周知的故事结束，关于Wesley Autrey，纽约地铁英雄。
cues.en: And I want to end with a known story about Wesley Autrey, New York subway hero.

cues.zh: 五十岁的非洲裔美国建筑工人站在地铁站台上。
cues.en: Fifty-year-old African-American construction worker standing on a subway.

cues.zh: 一个白人男子掉到了轨道上。
cues.en: A white guy falls on the tracks.

cues.zh: 地铁列车正在驶来。现场有75个人。
cues.en: The subway train is coming. There's 75 people there.

cues.zh: 你知道吗？他们都愣住了。
cues.en: You know what? They freeze.

cues.zh: 他完全有理由不插手。
cues.en: He's got a reason not to get involved.

cues.zh: 他是黑人，那家伙是白人，而且他还有两个孩子。
cues.en: He's black, the guy's white, and he's got two kids.

cues.zh: 但他却把孩子交给一个陌生人，
cues.en: Instead, he gives his kids to a stranger,

cues.zh: 跳下轨道，把那家伙安置在轨道之间，
cues.en: jumps on the tracks, puts the guy between the tracks,

cues.zh: 趴在他身上，地铁列车从他们上方驶过。
cues.en: lays on him, the subway goes over him.

cues.zh: Wesley和那家伙——高度只有20.5英寸。
cues.en: Wesley and the guy -- 20 and a half inches height.

cues.zh: 列车底部的间隙是21英寸。
cues.en: The train clearance is 21 inches.

cues.zh: 半英寸的差距就会削掉他的脑袋。
cues.en: A half an inch would have taken his head off.

cues.zh: 他说：“我做了任何人都会做的事，”跳下轨道没什么大不了的。
cues.en: And he said, "I did what anyone could do," no big deal to jump on the tracks.

cues.zh: 而道德上的责任是：“我做了每个人都应该做的事。”
cues.en: And the moral imperative is "I did what everyone should do."

cues.zh: 所以有一天，你会面临一个新的情况。
cues.en: And so one day, you will be in a new situation.

cues.zh: 走第一条路，你会成为恶的施害者。
cues.en: Take path one, you're going to be a perpetrator of evil.

cues.zh: 恶，意味着你会成为安达信那样。
cues.en: Evil, meaning you're going to be Arthur Andersen.

cues.zh: 你会作弊，或者纵容霸凌。
cues.en: You're going to cheat, or you're going to allow bullying.

cues.zh: 第二条路，你会犯下消极不作为的恶。
cues.en: Path two, you become guilty of the evil of passive inaction.

cues.zh: 第三条路，你会成为英雄。
cues.en: Path three, you become a hero.

cues.zh: 关键是，我们是否准备好走上颂扬平凡英雄的路，
cues.en: The point is, are we ready to take the path to celebrating ordinary heroes,

cues.zh: 等待合适的时机出现，
cues.en: waiting for the right situation to come along

cues.zh: 把英雄的想象力付诸行动？
cues.en: to put heroic imagination into action?

cues.zh: 因为这可能一生只有一次，
cues.en: Because it may only happen once in your life,

cues.zh: 当你错过它，你会永远知道，
cues.en: and when you pass it by, you'll always know,

cues.zh: 我本可以成为英雄，却让它从我身边溜走了。
cues.en: I could have been a hero and I let it pass me by.

cues.zh: 所以关键是先想到，然后去做。
cues.en: So the point is thinking it and then doing it.

cues.zh: 所以我要感谢你们。谢谢。
cues.en: So I want to thank you. Thank you.

cues.zh: 让我们在国内外共同对抗邪恶系统的力量，
cues.en: Let's oppose the power of evil systems at home and abroad,

cues.zh: 并把注意力放在积极的一面。
cues.en: and let's focus on the positive.

cues.zh: 倡导尊重个人尊严，追求正义与和平，
cues.en: Advocate for respect of personal dignity, for justice and peace,

cues.zh: 遗憾的是，我们的政府一直未能做到这一点。
cues.en: which sadly our administration has not been doing.

cues.zh: 非常感谢。
cues.en: Thanks so much.

cues.zh: （掌声）
cues.en: (Applause)
